items.title: AI governance & quality
items.goal: Every AI call in the portal is traceable — logged with its input, model, version, cost and duration — and every release is gated on the PRD's quality bar, measured against a recruiter-verified answer key with English and Chinese graded separately. AI spending cannot run away, and scoring and flags pass a fairness review.
prd: AI governance → requirement 1: every score, flag and parsed field shows the text it was based on → proposed
AI governance → requirement 2: each AI output is stored with its input, model version and date → proposed
AI governance → requirement 4: recruiters grade the AI on the sample set, English and Chinese separately → decided
AI governance → requirement 5: the approach follows Singapore's voluntary Model AI Governance Framework → proposed
Goals → MVP quality bar: at least 90% of parsed fields correct and 80% top-5 agreement → decided
Security (suggested) → a Vercel firewall rate-limits the AI routes and the provider has a monthly spend cap → suggested
AI pipeline → Quality: a script scores the parser and matcher against the answer key before each release → suggested
exit: Every AI service writes an `ai_runs` row with model, version, prompt version, cost and duration
The answer key exists, is recruiter-verified, and unverified entries are excluded from the bar
`npm run eval` reports field accuracy and top-5 agreement for English and Chinese separately and fails below the bar
A monthly spend cap check and per-route rate limits are in place
A fairness review of scoring and flags is recorded with its findings raised as issues
outOfScope: AI that rejects, advances or contacts anyone — an explicit non-goal
Model training or fine-tuning on candidate data
Grading against real CVs — the MVP grades the fictional sample set only
Adding scoring on Workplace Fairness Act attributes before the compliance review decides

items.title: Every AI call is traceable
items.story: As the agency director, I want to be able to see what the AI was asked, which model answered and what it cost, so that a result can be checked months later rather than taken on faith.
ac: Given any AI call in the app, when it completes or fails, then a row in `ai_runs` records what it read, the model and version, the prompt version, the output, the cost and the duration.
Given an AI output, when it is stored, then it has been validated against its schema first.
Given a new AI service is added without using the shared wrapper, when tests run, then the omission is caught.
prd: AI governance → requirement 2: each AI output is stored with its input, model version and date → proposed
Technical architecture → AI access: Vercel AI SDK, so the provider can be picked or switched without a rewrite → proposed
AI pipeline → every AI step returns JSON checked against a fixed schema → suggested
Data model → ai_runs → suggested

items.title: Build the shared runAi wrapper with schema validation and ai_runs logging
items.what: Build the one wrapper every AI call in the app goes through: provider-agnostic through the Vercel AI SDK, validating output against a Zod schema, and writing an `ai_runs` row with the input reference, model, version, prompt version, output, cost and duration — on failure as well as on success. Test-first with a fake model.
scope: `src/server/ai/run.ts`: takes a prompt, a schema and an input reference; returns validated output

Failing tests first with a fake model: a valid call writes a complete run row; a schema-invalid response is rejected and still writes a failed run; a provider error writes a failed run with its reason; cost and duration are always recorded
A fake model helper for unit tests, so no unit test ever reaches the network
A test that fails if an AI call is made outside this wrapper
exclusions: Any specific prompt
The rate limit and spend cap (E11-S04-T01)
Choosing a provider
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover success, schema failure, provider error, and cost and duration recording
A failed call still produces an `ai_runs` row with its reason
A test detects an AI call made outside the wrapper
No unit test makes a network call

items.title: The answer key is ready and human-verified
items.story: As a recruiter grading the AI in December, I want the correct answers agreed in advance and checked by a person, so that the quality bar measures the AI rather than measuring another AI.
ac: Given the sample CVs, when the answer key is drafted, then every entry is keyed by the file's SHA-256 and holds the expected parsed fields.
Given the sample jobs, when the key is drafted, then each has an expected top five candidates.
Given an entry a recruiter has not verified, when the eval runs, then that entry is excluded from the quality bar and reported as unverified.
prd: AI governance → requirement 4: recruiters grade the AI on the sample set against the quality bar, English and Chinese separately → decided
AI pipeline → Quality: a script scores the parser and matcher against the sample answer key → suggested
Sample data → the answer key contains only fictional people, so it may be committed

items.title: Draft the parsed-field answer key for the sample CVs
items.what: Draft the expected parsed fields for each sample CV, in the format the eval plan fixes, keyed by the file's SHA-256 and marked unverified until a recruiter confirms it. The CVs are fictional, so the key may be committed.
scope: `eval/answer-key/cvs/` with one entry per sample CV, keyed by SHA-256
Expected values for the approved profile fields, including total years computed from the work history
Each entry marked unverified with a slot for the verifying recruiter and date
English and Simplified Chinese CVs both covered, labelled by language so the eval can grade them separately
A note of any CV whose correct answer is genuinely ambiguous, so a recruiter decides rather than the draft
exclusions: Verifying the key — that is the recruiters' job (T03)
The top-5 key (T02)
Any real person's data, or any file name or URL from the sample-data store
done: Every sample CV available at drafting time has an entry keyed by its SHA-256
Every entry is marked unverified and names the language of its CV
Ambiguous cases are listed for a recruiter rather than guessed
No sample-data store URL and no real personal data appear in the committed key
verify: git diff | grep -iE 'blob.vercel-storage' # must be empty

items.title: Draft the expected top-5 candidates for each sample job
items.what: Draft, for each sample job, the five candidates a recruiter should reasonably rank highest, with a short reason each, in the eval plan's format and marked unverified until recruiters confirm.
scope: `eval/answer-key/jobs/` with one entry per sample job, keyed by the job description file's SHA-256
Five expected candidates per job, each identified by their CV's SHA-256, with a one-line reason
Each entry marked unverified with a slot for the verifying recruiter and date
Jobs whose sample set cannot supply five plausible candidates flagged rather than padded
exclusions: Verification (T03)
Changing the matcher to agree with the key
Any real person's data or store URL
done: Every sample job available at drafting time has an entry keyed by SHA-256 with up to five expected candidates
Each expected candidate carries a one-line reason
Jobs with fewer than five plausible candidates are flagged, not padded
Every entry is marked unverified
verify: git diff | grep -iE 'blob.vercel-storage' # must be empty

items.title: Add the recruiter verification workflow and the verified flag
items.what: Give recruiters a way to confirm or correct each answer-key entry and record that verification, so the quality bar is computed only from entries a person has checked. Test-first: the exclusion rule decides whether a release passes.
scope: A verified flag per entry, with the recruiter's typed name and the date
A workflow for reviewing entries — a script, a simple screen or an editable file, chosen in the task's spec
Failing tests first: unverified entries are excluded from the bar and reported; a corrected entry replaces the draft; the verified count is reported alongside every result
A summary of coverage: how many entries are verified, by language
exclusions: Drafting the key (T01, T02)
The eval script itself (E11-S03-T01)
Verifying the entries — that is the recruiters' work
done: Failing-then-passing tests prove unverified entries are excluded from the bar and reported separately
Every verification records a typed name and a date
Every eval result reports how many entries were verified, split by language

items.title: Releases are gated by the quality bar
items.story: As the product owner, I want a release to be refused when the AI falls below the agreed bar in either language, so that a prompt change cannot quietly make Chinese CVs worse.
ac: Given the answer key, when `npm run eval` runs, then it reports parsed-field accuracy and top-5 agreement for English and Chinese separately.
Given either language falls below its bar, when the eval finishes, then it exits non-zero and names what failed.
Given a change to a prompt, parser or matcher, when the pull request runs CI, then the eval runs, or is skipped with a clear message when its secret is unavailable.
prd: Goals → MVP quality bar: at least 90% of parsed fields correct and 80% top-5 agreement, the same bar for English and Chinese → decided
AI governance → requirement 4: English and Chinese graded separately → decided
AI pipeline → Quality: a script scores the parser and matcher against the answer key before each release → suggested

items.title: Build npm run eval with separate English and Chinese grading
items.what: Build the quality script the PRD requires: run the real parser and matcher over the sample set, compare against the verified answer key, and report field accuracy and top-5 agreement for English and Chinese separately, failing below 90% and 80%. Test-first: the scoring rules decide releases.
scope: `npm run eval` producing a JSON result and a Markdown report
Field accuracy and top-5 agreement computed per the eval plan's rules
English and Chinese scored separately against the same bar, with the counts behind each figure

Failing tests first for the scoring functions using fixed fixtures: a field just above and just below the bar; a top-5 with a tie; an unverified entry excluded; an empty language set reported rather than passing by default
A non-zero exit and a clear message when either language misses its bar
exclusions: Drafting or verifying the answer key
Running against real CVs
Tuning prompts to pass — findings are raised as issues
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the bar boundary, ties, exclusion of unverified entries and the empty-set case
The report shows English and Chinese figures separately with the counts behind them
A language below its bar makes the script exit non-zero and name the failure
An empty or fully unverified language set is reported as not measured rather than passing

items.title: Run the eval in CI on prompt, parser and matcher changes
items.what: Add the CI workflow that runs the eval when a pull request touches a prompt, the parser or the matcher, gated on the provider secret so forks and secretless runs skip cleanly instead of failing.
scope: .github/workflows/eval.yml with path filters on the prompt, parser and matcher folders
A guard that skips with an explanatory message when the provider secret is unavailable
The Markdown report posted as a job summary and uploaded as an artifact
A note in the workflow of the approximate cost of a run, since it makes real model calls
exclusions: Running the eval on every pull request — it costs money
Storing any secret in the repository
Gating on anything other than the documented bar
done: A pull request touching a prompt triggers the workflow; one touching unrelated code does not
Without the provider secret, the job skips with a clear message and does not fail the pull request
The eval report appears as a job summary
The workflow's approximate cost per run is documented

items.title: AI costs cannot run away
items.story: As the agency director, I want a hard ceiling on what the portal can spend on AI, because anyone who finds the URL can use it and there is no sign-in to stop them.
ac: Given the AI routes, when they are called repeatedly from one source, then requests beyond the limit are rejected with a clear message.
Given the month's spend has reached the cap, when a new AI call is attempted, then it is refused and the refusal is visible to the recruiter and in the logs.
Given the cap is reached, when a recruiter uses the portal, then everything that does not need an AI call still works.
prd: Security (suggested) → a Vercel firewall rate-limits the AI routes and the provider has a monthly spend cap; without sign-in anyone with the link could run up costs → suggested
Data model → ai_runs records cost per call → suggested
Users → no sign-in in the MVP → decided

items.title: Add the per-route rate limit check and the monthly spend cap
items.what: Add the in-app half of cost control: a monthly spend cap computed from `ai_runs` that refuses further AI calls once reached, and an application-level rate limit behind the Vercel firewall rule. Test-first, and the portal must stay usable without AI when the cap is hit.
scope: A spend check in the shared AI wrapper, summing the month's cost from `ai_runs` against a configured cap

Failing tests first: under the cap the call proceeds; at the cap it is refused with a clear reason; the refusal is recorded; non-AI pages still work when the cap is reached; the month boundary uses Singapore time
An application-level per-route limit complementing the firewall rule
A recruiter-facing message explaining why an AI feature is unavailable
exclusions: The Vercel firewall rule itself (E01-S04-T02)
Setting a real budget figure with the provider
Billing integration
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover under cap, at cap, the recorded refusal, the Singapore month boundary and continued non-AI use
Reaching the cap produces a clear recruiter-facing message, not a stack trace
The cap value comes from configuration, never hard-coded

items.title: Scoring and flags pass a fairness review
items.story: As the agency director, I want an independent check that our scoring and flags behave the way we promised, so that we can show a client or a regulator how the portal reaches a number.
ac: Given the built scoring path, when it is reviewed, then every protected attribute the PRD names is proven excluded, by test rather than by assertion.
Given the gap check's fair-employment flags, when they are reviewed, then they match the TAFEP attributes the PRD names and nothing more.
Given the review, when it finds a problem, then it is raised as a GitHub issue rather than fixed silently inside the review.
prd: AI governance → requirement 3: protected attributes are handled as listed under Job matching → decided
AI governance → requirement 5: the approach follows Singapore's voluntary Model AI Governance Framework → proposed
Fair employment → TAFEP attributes; Workplace Fairness Act from end-2027, with four attributes not yet covered → noted
Data, privacy & compliance → Risk 1: no sign-in, accepted for the MVP → decided

items.title: Run the fairness and AI governance review and raise its findings
items.what: Review the built scoring, gap-check and search paths against the PRD guardrails, the compliance baseline and Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework, and raise every finding as its own issue rather than fixing it inside the review.
scope: Evidence-based review: for each protected attribute, name the test that proves it is excluded
Fair-employment flags checked against the TAFEP attributes the PRD names, with the four Workplace Fairness Act attributes recorded as a future decision rather than added
Model AI Governance Framework practices: traceability, human oversight, explainability and the suggestion-only rule, each mapped to what the code does
The MVP's accepted risks restated with what changes at the real-data release
Findings written to `docs/compliance/review-mvp.md` and raised as issues
exclusions: Fixing findings in this task
Legal advice or sign-off
Adding scoring on any attribute
done: Every protected attribute the PRD names has a test cited as proof of exclusion, or a finding if it does not
Fair-employment flags are confirmed to match the named TAFEP attributes and nothing more
Every finding is raised as a GitHub issue and linked from the review
The review states what must change before real CVs are loaded
